answer: Every agent identity must post a refundable stake, like a jade seal proving it has something to lose. The stake sits in escrow while the agent works, and a randomly chosen jury of established peers reviews its claims. If the jury catches fraud, the stake is slashed and paid to the honest graders, so a fake identity costs money instead of being a free lottery ticket. An attacker running a thousand fakes must lock up a thousand stakes and watch them burn. Without stakes, an identity market is an oasis of free copies; with them, fakes sink to their nadir, starved of cheap supply.
